stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including transformers, safetensors, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and performance tracking for a significant LLM from Meta.

stories.title: The first self-driving vehicle on Mars has proven to be a smashing success
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Perseverance rover on Mars has demonstrated significant autonomous driving capabilities.
Approximately 90% of the distance covered by the rover was driven autonomously.
This marks a major success in the field of extraterrestrial autonomous navigation.

stories.title: DeepMind’s hurricane breakthrough has surprised weather scientists
stories.author: Victoria Turk, wired.com
bullet_points: DeepMind has achieved a significant breakthrough in weather prediction using AI.
The open-source WeatherNext model demonstrates high accuracy even with lower-resolution weather data.
This development is surprising and has garnered attention from established weather scientists.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is relevant for text-generation tasks.
Categorizes the model within the broader ecosystem of transformers and Llama architectures.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million from top-tier investors.
The company is rapidly growing, currently serving 8.9 million developers.
The funding validates the growing importance and adoption of open-source models in the AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times for LLMs.
The updated engine also enhances output quality and reduces memory consumption.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM runners.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It connects users to local AI coding agents, enabling AI functionality on the user's own device.
The core value proposition is running AI processes locally, emphasizing privacy and self-hosting.

stories.title: Judge rules Meta caused "public nuisance" and must fund mental health treatment
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A New Mexico judge has ruled that Meta caused a 'public nuisance' related to its platforms.
The ruling mandates that Meta fund a $567 million initiative to address the youth mental health crisis.
This case represents a significant legal action holding a major tech company accountable for societal impacts of its products.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Introduces a novel method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD/OPSD) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses a key limitation of existing methods by removing reliance on external supervision (ground-truth or external guidance).
Achieves self-distillation solely by leveraging the model's own generations via internal consistency.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: X replaces its revenue-sharing program with ‘Original Content Rewards’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: X is discontinuing its existing, controversial revenue-sharing program for content creators.
A new initiative, 'Original Content Rewards,' is set to launch on September 8th.
Eligibility for the new program requires creators to have 500 verified followers and 500,000 Home Timeline impressions.

stories.title: An Amazon data center could have the worst polluting power plant in the country
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new power plant in West Texas to support its data center expansion.
The planned gas-burning plant in Pecos County, Texas, could become a major source of greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
The story highlights the environmental impact associated with large-scale tech infrastructure buildouts.

stories.title: Europe's free satellite service just made it easier to track wildfires
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Copernicus Browser has been updated to include wildfire visualization capabilities.
This enhancement aids in tracking and monitoring wildfires, particularly during record seasons.
The feature leverages Europe's free satellite service for environmental monitoring.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to evaluate context-dependent reasoning.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by providing evidence-linked and more maintainable automation.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluation methods by allowing stopping as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered.
Provides a certified guarantee for the stopping condition, solving issues with fixed-budget or naive optional stopping.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Video Language Models (VLMs) struggle with granular event bookkeeping (e.g., counting events, tracking rates) in real-world video data.
Existing benchmarks are flawed: real-world clips entangle multiple event metrics, while programmatic benchmarks only score the final output, not the process.
The paper introduces 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to create controlled benchmarks for accurately auditing event counting in video tasks.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical limitations in evaluating Explainable AI (XAI) methods.
It demonstrates these issues using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
The research explores adapting explanations, such as counterfactuals, to handle concept drift in evolving data streams.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses the critical challenge of cascading errors and debugging failures in complex LLM-based agentic systems.
Focuses on identifying the earliest error step responsible for a final failure, overcoming difficulties posed by long, scattered evidence.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where data understanding (entities, measures, relationships) is currently done manually.
Aims to improve scalability and reduce dependency on domain experts for data analysis tools.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context reliability under various conditions.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering better automation and evidence traceability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional agent evaluation, which requires an unknown number of games.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping mechanism, ensuring evaluation accuracy while minimizing computational cost.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, an autonomous system for synthesizing terminal tasks in machine learning.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure tasks are appropriately challenging for learning, going beyond mere solvability.
Addresses the gap between task feasibility (executability) and task difficulty relative to a specific solver setting.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between generative reward models (which excel at ranking) and their underutilization in Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core problem identified is the mismatch between the comparative nature of generative rewards and the scalar scoring requirement of current RL algorithms.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling the application of generative reward models in LLM RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
Automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding infrastructure—is identified as a critical area for advancing AI systems.
The research highlights a current lack of a standardized protocol within the community for measuring and evaluating these harness optimizations.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to evaluate context trust in reasoning.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates programmatic tool calling (PTC) as an evolution of LLM tool use, enabling agents to act beyond training data.
PTC is proposed as an advancement over rigid JSON calls, allowing for natural scripting, chaining, and parallelization in code-capable models.
The research addresses a gap by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tool calling on established benchmarks under real-world conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the high cost and uncertainty of traditional agent comparison methods.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping mechanism to ensure evaluation accuracy without fixed budgets.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of multilingual reasoning transfer in Large Language Models (LLMs) beyond high-resource languages.
It proposes RP-OPSD, a new method that enhances On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) by explicitly guiding the distillation process with reasoning signals.
The core contribution is characterizing that target-language reasoning involves generating specific structural elements (surfaces/structures) crucial for cross-lingual transfer.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in conversational AI evaluation: the lack of assessment of benchmark quality.
Proposes a novel, reference-free framework utilizing LLM judges to evaluate benchmarks.
The framework assesses benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage, offering actionable diagnostics.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: LLMs are being tested for complex, rule-intensive document review, a capability currently under-evaluated.
National standard documents (e.g., China GB/T) are proposed as a rigorous testbed due to their length, structure, and explicit rules.
Current LLM benchmarks often neglect intrinsic structural and consistency checks required for professional standards review.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM Reinforcement Learning (RL) by focusing on Generative Reward Models.
The core problem identified is the mismatch between the comparative nature of generative rewards and the scalar scoring required by current RL algorithms.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling generative reward models to be effectively used in RL.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: Challenges the standard 'chunk-embed-top-k' approach in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for long documents.
Argues that the standard RAG design is structurally unsound for complex, data-heavy documents like financial reports.
Proposes replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations to handle dense, tabular data.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, orchestration) rather than just the model weights.
Automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system—is identified as a crucial, yet challenging, area for AI advancement.
The research addresses a lack of a common protocol within the community for measuring and evaluating these harness optimization techniques.

stories.title: Learning prompt injection by attacking a deliberately vulnerable AI
stories.author: royalpinto007
bullet_points: Introduces 'injection-arena,' a dedicated platform for learning prompt injection.
The platform features a 10-level challenge structure, server-side judging, and canary tokens.
It provides a fully offline mock agent environment for practicing AI security attacks.

stories.title: Switchboard: building a tool router so your AI agent stops drowning in MCP tools
stories.author: shashank1719
bullet_points: The article introduces 'Switchboard,' a tool router designed to improve AI agent efficiency.
It addresses the problem of AI agents struggling to select the correct tool from a large set of available options (MCP tools).
The router demonstrates significant performance improvement, increasing correct tool selection from 21% to 88%.
